content:
julia: FYI dashboard chart p95 up ~2.8x since canary deploy last night. noticed during sync, digging now — looks like a render / bundle change

mike: ugh. which chart? whole dashboard or specific widgets?

julia: heatmap and metric grid mostly. small ones ok. heatmap frame times jump when multiple layers visible. repro on canary and local with canary bundle. link: https://console-canary/redwood/12345 (canary)

sara: any obvious bundle bloat from analyzer?

julia: ran analyzer quick: delta shows a new dependency pulled in -> analytics-shim (~130kb gz). suspect it prevents some tree-shaking. snippet:

```
Before: app.chunk.js.gz 720kb
After:  app.chunk.js.gz 855kb (+135kb)
Added modules:
 - analytics-shim/index.js (+78kb)
 - chart-serializer (+40kb)
```

mike: chart-serializer? we didn't change core renderer last night. that smells like a new import path/alias brought in by the rollout UX PR (alex?).

alex: I opened the PR, changed dynamic import to inline to fix SSR flash. didn't realize it pulled analytics-shim. my bad.

sam: inline import -> static include usually prevents tree-shake. can we lazy-load analytics-shim behind interaction?

alex: yeah. but SSR dev complained about jank so I inlined. tradeoff.

sara: besides size, why p95 spike? bigger bundles increase parse time but 2.8x seems larger than parse cost alone. any telemetry showing main-thread blocking?

julia: telemetry shows long task spikes at chart mount; stack points to serializer.workerInit -> polyfill detection -> synchronous require of analytics-shim. the shim runs some detection code on import.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-20T22:06 finished for tag dashboard-rollout-v6 (3 instances).

mike: if shim runs detection on import, moving to async import should avoid blocking main thread during mount. also could be KV-prefetch pressure if charts request extra metadata concurrently. check network waterfall?

julia: network isn't the blocker. it's main-thread parse + init from the shim. waterfall fine.

sara: two action items: (1) quick rollback of the canary or disable the inline change so tree-shake works, (2) longer term: add a lint rule to disallow sync imports of libs that do heavy init on module load for client bundles.

alex: I can patch a hotfix to lazy import the shim and push a canary rollback if we want.

sam: +1 hotfix. also let's add a microprobe metric: chart-mount-long-task to alert at 200ms. we missed this in rollout canary dashboards.

mike: agree. also check routing policy quotas — if graph-worker pool is overloaded it could cascade, but looks isolated to client CPU.

julia: patch plan: alex pushes lazy import change, I’ll run local analyzer and a quick canary (one host), if p95 drops we promote. target rollback window 30m.

alex: prepping PR now. small diff:

```js
// before
import analyticsShim from 'analytics-shim';

// after
let analyticsShim;
async function ensureShim(){
  if(!analyticsShim) analyticsShim = (await import('analytics-shim')).default;
}
// use ensureShim() on interaction instead of module init
```

sam: also add telemetry tag to the canary: rollout-tag=chart-inline-fix for easier dashboard filtering.

deploy-bot: rollback request received for canary dashboard-rollout-v6. initiating rollback to dashboard-rollout-v5 (stable).

julia: after rollback p95 dropped back to baseline in staging smoke. will watch prod canary once promoted.

mike: follow-ups for postmortem: - add rule to detect modules with side-effectful top-level code via static analysis - add an entry in rollout checklist: run bundle-analyzer on canary and compare top 10 modules - add perf probe for long tasks on key UI paths

sara: agree. I'll own the checklist update + lint rule proposal.

alex: sorry for the break — I'll avoid inline import unless tested.

sam: one more thing: telemetry sampling for canaries was lowered recently (we sample 10% by default). for perf regressions we should bump to 100% during canary windows. can we make that automatic?

mike: ops-team, can we toggle sampling for rollout-tag automatically?

ops-bot: ops-bot: Added feature request: auto-increase-telemetry-sampling-for-rollouts (#342). tagging eng-platform + eng-sre.

julia: temporary manual step: sam bumped sampling for the canary to 100% and we have enough traces to confirm.

sam: ok tests passing on hotfix, sending single-host canary now -> will post results in 15m.

(15m later)

sam: canary hotfix p95 back to normal on that host, no long tasks. rolling to remaining hosts.

mike: good. once fully rolled, let's close with a short postmortem and the checklist PR from sara. thanks team :thumbsup:

julia: filing a short incident note and timeline now.
